IBM.rationale: IBM is in severe fundamental distress following its July 14, 2026 profit warning and Q2 earnings miss. The stock crashed 25% in a single day—its worst day in 115-year history—erasing $68B in market cap. Q2 revenue grew only 1% YoY (vs. 5%+ guidance), with Infrastructure revenue declining 7% and Transaction Processing revenue down 9%. The core problem is structural: customers are shifting IT budgets away from IBM's software and mainframe offerings toward AI servers, memory chips, and storage hardware. Software growth decelerated sharply from 11% in Q1 to 5% in Q2, undermining the entire bull thesis of software-led transformation. Management cut full-year revenue guidance from 5%+ to 4%-5%, acknowledging they 'did not adapt and move quickly enough.' Multiple securities law investigations have been launched. The stock at $206.65 trades at P/E 18.4x—near the bottom of its 18-51x range—but this is not cheap given deteriorating fundamentals: YoY EPS declined 1.7%, net income fell 1.3%, and the competitive position is weakening as hyperscalers and hardware vendors capture AI infrastructure spend. Balance sheet leverage remains elevated at ~$62B debt. The near-term catalyst is negative: ongoing investigations, potential further guidance cuts, and the risk that the Q2 deal slippage represents a permanent share loss rather than deferred demand. News sentiment turned sharply negative in mid-July (scores of -0.714 on July 14-15). This is a deteriorating business with a broken growth narrative, expensive relative to its new reality, and facing credible downside catalysts.
